facts.text: Grayson Valley earned its name from the Grayson Lumber Company, a Birmingham‑based firm owned by the wealthy Grayson family in the mid‑20th century.
The area’s early history traces back to Alabama’s lumber boom of the late 1800s and early 1900s, when yellow pine demand spurred massive logging.
After World War II, Grayson Valley evolved from timberlands and farmland into a growing residential community, shaped by the Grayson Lumber Company’s extensive land holdings.
Geographically, Grayson Valley sits between Birmingham’s Spring Lake neighborhood and the suburbs of Clay, Trussville, and Center Point.
As an unincorporated community, Grayson Valley falls under Jefferson County’s jurisdiction rather than having its own municipal government.
Historical records for the area include railroad schedules and shipping guides that charted routes and commerce during the early 20th century.
